subtitle: DuckStation
_subtitle_source: subtitle names the backend the player will actually run, the same way 18 manifests say "BizHawk".
_platform_source: the world's own randomizer page: "This is an Archipelago implementation of the PlayStation 1 version of Spyro 2: Ripto's Rage (1999), not the Reignited Trilogy version (2018)."
_drafted_note: Drafted 2026-08-25 from the world's OWN repository -- its __init__.py, archipelago.json, setup guide and README, read that day. No field is filled in from memory or from what other games on the same console do.
_ap_world_name_source: READ FROM THE WORLD'S OWN CODE: apworld/spyro2/__init__.py sets `game = "Spyro 2"`, and the world's archipelago.json agrees: {"game": "Spyro 2"}. ⚠ NOT "Spyro 2: Ripto's Rage" -- the display name carries the subtitle and the AP slot name does not.
description: Spyro 2: Ripto's Rage as a multiworld. Talismans, orbs and -- depending on options -- gems, skill points and life bottles are shuffled across the session. Requires the player's own NTSC-U disc, and DuckStation with Execution Mode set to Interpreter.
_description_source: written by us from the world's own structure and its setup guide's stated requirements. No text is copied from the game.
_checks_verified_note: FALSE. Nobody has played this. For a kind=world game the checks travel through the WORLD'S client, not through London -- so what is unproven here is not a RAM map of ours (there is none) but the whole chain: apworld installs, emulator starts over the bridge, the world's client attaches and carries a check. London warns at launch while this is false, which is exactly right until a tester reports one.
_requires_source: PSX title. The setup guide lists it among the player's own requirements: "A legal US Spyro 2: Ripto's Rage ROM. We cannot help with this step."

rom.description: Your own Spyro 2: Ripto's Rage disc image for PlayStation 1 -- the NTSC-U (North American) release
rom._description_source: the setup guide, word for word: "A legal US Spyro 2: Ripto's Rage ROM." The randomizer page states why the region matters: NTSC-U is required "due to differences in the internal workings of the game".
rom._hash_note: No hash is claimed. The guide states none.

emulator.name: DuckStation
emulator._source: the setup guide names "[Duckstation]" without a version, and calls it the option "tested more for Spyro 2 by the community". ⚠ The guide also supports BizHawk 2.9.1/2.10 as an alternative -- see _emulator_alternative_note.

client.name: Spyro 2 Archipelago Client (S2AP.Desktop.exe)
client._name_source: the setup guide names it: "Open S2AP.Desktop.exe, the Spyro 2 client." It is shipped in the s2ap .zip beside the apworld on the same release.
client._kind_source: the world ships its OWN client -- a separate desktop application, distributed as the s2ap .zip asset on every release beside spyro2.apworld, and the setup guide's entire connect sequence runs through it: "Open S2AP.Desktop.exe, the Spyro 2 client ... Enter your host, slot ... Click Connect." The guide makes it mandatory for the DuckStation path: "If you are playing on Duckstation, you also need the Client (within the s2ap .zip file)." Same shape, same author and same client family as spyro3, already in this catalogue. London must NOT read memory for this game.
client._protocol_source: extensions/duckstation/extension.json declares {"protocol": "duckstation"} and its Systems are ["PSX", "PS1"]. The setup guide's DuckStation path is the one this manifest describes, and it requires a specific emulator setting -- Settings > Game Properties > Console > Execution Mode = Interpreter -- which is carried in the description because nothing else reaches the player.
client._lua_note: No Lua. The world's desktop client attaches to DuckStation itself; there is no connector script for London to load.

apworld._source: the author's own releases page; the newest release read 25 Aug 2026 is 2.1.0, carrying both spyro2.apworld and s2ap-v2-1-0.zip (the client).
apworld._world_version_source: the world's archipelago.json: {"world_version": "2.1.0"}, matching the newest release tag.
apworld._minimum_ap_version_source: the world's archipelago.json: {"minimum_ap_version": "0.6.1"}, agreeing with the setup guide's "version 0.6.1 or later". Our client is 0.6.7, so this is satisfied.

_patch_extension_source: read from the world's own source, 25 Aug 2026: the 12 .py files in apworld/spyro2 were searched. Rom.py defines an `APProcedurePatch` and a result_file_ending, but NO `APPatchExtension` -- no custom Python patch steps exist for London's patcher to refuse.
_patch_note: There is deliberately NO `patch` block. This is a kind=world game: the world's own client owns whatever patching happens, and London never patches for it.

world_by.name: Uroogla, Garmo, PhoenixAki and Sonofkrom
world_by._authors_source: the world names them itself: archipelago.json {"authors": ["Uroogla", "Garmo", "PhoenixAki", "Sonofkrom"]}.
world_by._source: the repository the world is published from; its own source, archipelago.json and setup guide are what this manifest was written against.
world_by._licence_source: the GitHub API reports spdx_id MIT for the repository, which carries a LICENSE file (25 Aug 2026).

credits._game_by_note: Not recorded rather than guessed. The game is the property of its publisher and is never distributed here; the player supplies their own copy. The Archipelago world is its authors' work. Only the plugin itself is by solida1987.

_emulator_alternative_note: The setup guide supports TWO emulators: DuckStation (with the world's own S2AP.Desktop.exe client) and BizHawk 2.9.1/2.10 (with Archipelago's BizHawk Client, driven by the world's Client.py, which subclasses BizHawkClient). This manifest describes the DuckStation path, because it is the one the guide says is "tested more for Spyro 2 by the community" and because it matches spyro3's shape. A player who prefers BizHawk can still follow the world's guide by hand; London simply is not driving that path.
